conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really challenging and overwhelming time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you every step of the way. 

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to get a better understanding of how you're feeling and to see if there's anything we can do to support you during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a really important part of making sure you're getting the care you need right now.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I want you to feel safe and supported throughout our conversation. My goal is to create a space where you feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings, without fear of judgment. 

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional well-being over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this process as comfortable and straightforward as possible. 

So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, it's been really hard for me to laugh and find the humor in things like I used to. I mean, I still enjoy some things, like watching my baby smile or playing with them, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and even when I do find something funny, it's just not as funny as it used to be. I've noticed that I've been feeling really tired and low-energy, which makes it even harder to enjoy things. And sometimes, when I'm feeling overwhelmed, I get these anxious thoughts about my baby's safety, and it's hard to calm myself down. It's like, I know I'm a good mom, but these thoughts just keep popping up, and it's hard to shake them off. 

I'd say maybe once or twice this past week, I've had a moment where I felt a little more like myself, and I was able to laugh and enjoy something, but it's fleeting. Most of the time, I just feel sad and discouraged, and I don't know how to get out of this funk. Even when I try to do things I used to enjoy, like reading or taking a walk, I just can't seem to find the pleasure in it like I used to. And at night, I have trouble falling asleep because my mind starts racing with all these worries, and I wake up a few times feeling anxious. It's been really tough, and I just feel like I'm not doing anything right. Sometimes, I even cry when I'm feeling stressed, like once or twice a week, and it's just really hard to cope with all these emotions.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I wouldn't say that's been me, unfortunately. Like I said, it's been hard for me to find the humor in things and laugh like I used to. I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, and even when I do try to laugh or find the funny side of things, it feels forced. I'm just not feeling like myself, and it's hard to explain. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and they'll do something cute, but instead of laughing, I just feel this overwhelming sense of responsibility and worry. It's like, I'm happy to see them happy, but I'm just not feeling that joy myself. And that makes me feel guilty, like I'm not being the mom I'm supposed to be. Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like so much work. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or trying new restaurants, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of my baby, and I don't have the energy or motivation to do much else. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, but then I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the things I need to do to take care of my baby, and I'll just end up staying home and feeling stuck. 

It's hard to explain, but even when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, it just doesn't feel the same. I'll be doing it, but my mind will be elsewhere, worrying about my baby or feeling anxious about something. And then I'll start to feel guilty, like I'm not being a good mom because I'm not enjoying the things I'm doing with my baby. It's just really hard to find pleasure in things right now, and it's making me feel really sad and discouraged. Sometimes I have these fleeting thoughts of self-harm, but they're not constant, and I don't have any plan or intent to act on them. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm just trying to survive each day, and I'm not really living.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that sounds like me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If my baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm feeling tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. I just feel like I'm constantly making mistakes and that I'm not good enough as a mom. It's like, I'll be trying to take care of my baby, and something will go wrong, and I'll just immediately think, "Oh, this is my fault. I should have done this differently." 

And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to pack something in the diaper bag, I'll think, "What kind of mom forgets that?" or if my baby isn't sleeping well, I'll think, "This is because I'm not establishing a good routine." It's just this constant self-doubt and self-blame, and it's really hard to shake off. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeling overwhelmed and anxious, and I'll just start crying because I feel like I'm not doing anything right. And then I'll feel guilty for crying, because I think I should be stronger and more capable. It's just a really hard cycle to break. 

I also have trouble sleeping, which doesn't help. I'll wake up in the middle of the night, thinking about all the things I could be doing better, and it's hard to calm myself down. And when I'm feeling really stressed, I sometimes have these anxious thoughts about my baby's safety, and it's hard to stop them. But, despite all these feelings and thoughts, I've been able to get up and take care of my baby every day, even when it feels like everything is too much. That's something, right?
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me. I feel like I'm always worried about something, even when everything seems to be going okay. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or playing with them, and suddenly I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if my baby gets sick? What if I'm not doing enough to stimulate their development? What if something happens to me and I'm not there to take care of them? 

It's just this constant, nagging sense of anxiety that I don't know how to shake off. Sometimes I'll be awake at night, feeding my baby or changing their diaper, and I'll just start to feel this overwhelming sense of worry. My mind will start racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll feel like I'm going to be sick. It's hard to explain, but it's like my brain just can't turn off, and I'm stuck in this cycle of worry and fear. 

And it's not just about my baby, either. Sometimes I'll worry about little things, like whether the house is clean enough or whether I'm making healthy enough meals. It's just this constant sense of unease, like I'm always waiting for something to go wrong. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always on edge, always waiting for the other shoe to drop. 

Sometimes, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed, I'll have these fleeting thoughts of self-harm, but they're not constant, and I don't have any plan or intent to act on them. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm just trying to survive each day, and I'm not really living. I'm trying to manage without turning to substances, but it's hard when I feel like I'm drowning in all these emotions. I'm just trying to cope, one day at a time.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding my baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to be sick. It's like, I'll be fine one minute, and the next, I'll just be overwhelmed with this sense of fear and anxiety. 

It's hard to explain, but it's like my body just takes over, and I'm not in control anymore. I'll start to feel like I'm going to lose control, like I'm going to pass out or something. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes I'll be with my partner or family members, and I'll just feel this sense of panic come over me. It's embarrassing, because I don't know how to explain it, and I don't want to worry them. 

But it's not just the panic attacks, either. I've also been having these anxious thoughts about my baby's safety, and it's hard to stop them. I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll think, "What if something happens to my baby?" or "What if I'm not doing enough to protect them?" And then I'll start to feel this sense of panic and worry, and it's hard to calm myself down. 

I've been trying to manage my anxiety by taking deep breaths and trying to focus on the present moment, but it's hard when I'm feeling overwhelmed. Sometimes I'll cry when I'm feeling stressed, like once or twice a week, and it's just really hard to cope with all these emotions. I feel guilty for feeling this way, like I'm not being a good mom because I'm not in control of my emotions. But at the same time, I'm trying to be kind to myself, because I know that I'm doing the best I can. 

It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm walking around with this constant sense of fear and anxiety, and I don't know how to make it stop. I feel like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and it's exhausting. I'm trying to get through each day, but it's hard when I'm feeling like this. And sometimes, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious and worried, and it's hard to fall back asleep. I'll lie there, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and it's just really hard to calm myself down.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of my baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly trying to manage their needs, and I'm just not doing a good enough job. And then, on top of that, I've got all these other responsibilities, like household chores and cooking and laundry... it just feels like too much. 

I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibility, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. I'll be trying to do one thing, and then I'll think about all the other things I need to do, and it just feels overwhelming. I'll start to feel anxious and worried, and then I'll just feel like I'm going to break down. 

And it's not just the practical things, either. Emotionally, I'm just feeling really drained. I'm trying to navigate all these new feelings and emotions, and it's hard. I'm feeling guilty and ashamed and anxious, and I don't know how to make it stop. I just feel like I'm not doing anything right, and that I'm failing as a mom. 

Sometimes, I'll just sit there, feeling like I'm at my breaking point, and I'll think, "I don't know how much more of this I can take." But then I'll look at my baby, and I'll think, "I have to keep going, for them." So I'll take a deep breath, and I'll try to keep going, but it's hard. Really hard. And sometimes, I'll have these fleeting thoughts of self-harm, but they're not constant, and I don't have any plan or intent to act on them. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm just trying to survive each day, and I'm not really living.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because I'm getting up to feed my baby. Even when I do get a chance to sleep, I just can't seem to relax. My mind starts racing, and I'll think about all the things that are worrying me, and I'll just lie there, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. 

I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just feel this sense of dread, like something is wrong. And then I'll start to think about all the things that could go wrong, and it's just hard to calm myself down. I'll try to take deep breaths, and I'll try to focus on the present moment, but it's hard when my mind is racing like that. 

And even when I do fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I'll wake up feeling tired and groggy, and it's just hard to face the day. I feel like I'm running on empty, and I don't know how to refill my tank. I'm just trying to get through each day, but it's hard when I'm feeling so exhausted and overwhelmed. 

I've also been having trouble falling asleep because I'll start to think about all the things I need to do the next day, and I'll feel anxious about not being able to get everything done. Or I'll start to worry about my baby's health, or my own health, and it's just hard to quiet my mind. I'll try to remind myself that everything is okay, and that I'm doing the best I can, but it's hard to shake off those feelings of anxiety and worry. 

It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm stuck in this cycle of unhappiness and anxiety, and I don't know how to break free. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really living. And it's hard, because I want to be happy, and I want to enjoy this time with my baby, but it's just not happening right now.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I'm supposed to be happy, right? I just had a baby, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my new little one. But the truth is, I'm just not feeling it. I'm feeling overwhelmed, and anxious, and just really, really sad. 

I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll think about all the things that I'm not doing right, and all the things that I'm worried about, and it just feels like too much. I'll start to cry, and I won't be able to stop. It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed with emotions, and I don't know how to process them. 

And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too. Like, I'll be trying to get my baby to sleep, and they'll just refuse to settle down, and I'll feel this sense of frustration and sadness. Or I'll be trying to make a meal, and I'll just feel so overwhelmed by all the things I need to do, and I'll start to cry. 

I feel like I'm just walking around in a fog, and I don't know how to get out of it. I'll try to talk to my partner, or my friends, but they just don't get it. They'll say things like, "Oh, you're just tired," or "You're just adjusting to motherhood," but it's more than that. It's like, I'm losing myself in all of this, and I don't know how to find my way back. 

Sometimes, I'll have a good day, and I'll think, "Okay, maybe I'm turning a corner," but then the next day will come, and I'll be right back to feeling sad and miserable. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm stuck in this cycle of sadness, and I don't know how to break free. I've been crying once or twice a week, and it's just really hard to cope with all these emotions. And sometimes, I'll have these fleeting thoughts of self-harm, but they're not constant, and I don't have any plan or intent to act on them. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm just trying to survive each day, and I'm not really living.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just when I'm feeling overwhelmed or frustrated. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness, and I'll start to cry. It's like, I'm just so emotional all the time, and I don't know how to control it. 

I'll be feeding my baby, or changing their diaper, or just sitting there holding them, and I'll just start to cry. It's like, I'm just so happy to have them, but at the same time, I'm just so sad and overwhelmed. I feel like I'm just losing myself in all of this, and I don't know how to find my way back. 

Sometimes, I'll try to hold it in, and I'll just feel this lump in my throat, and I'll try to swallow it down. But other times, I'll just let it all out, and I'll cry and cry and cry. It's like, I'm just so tired of feeling this way, and I don't know how to make it stop. 

I've been crying a lot, like once or twice a week, and it's just really hard to cope with all these emotions. I feel like I'm just so emotional all the time, and I don't know how to control it. I'll be talking to my partner, or my friends, and I'll just start to cry, and it's just really embarrassing. 

I just wish I could be happy, and carefree, and just enjoy this time with my baby. But it's just not happening right now. I'm just so sad, and overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. I've been trying to manage my anxiety and sadness, but it's hard when I'm feeling so exhausted and drained all the time. I've been getting up every day to take care of my baby, but it's just hard to find the energy to do anything else.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I don't know if I should be saying this, but... yes. The thought of harming myself has occurred to me. It's not something that I've thought about a lot, but it's been there, lingering in the back of my mind. It's like, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and sad, and I don't know how to make it stop, I'll just think, "What if I just...?" And then I'll push the thought away, because it's not something that I want to think about. 

But it's scary, because it's like, I don't know where that thought is coming from. I don't know why I'm thinking it, or what it means. And it's hard to talk about, because I don't want anyone to worry about me. But at the same time, I feel like I need to be honest, because maybe that's the only way that I can get help. 

It's not like I have a plan or anything. It's just... it's like, when I'm feeling really desperate, and I don't know how to make it stop, that thought will occur to me. And it's terrifying, because I don't know what it means, or what I'm capable of. 

I've been trying to manage my anxiety and sadness, but it's hard when I'm feeling so exhausted and drained all the time. I've been getting up every day to take care of my baby, but it's just hard to find the energy to do anything else. And sometimes, I'll have these fleeting thoughts of self-harm, but they're not constant, and I don't have any plan or intent to act on them. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm just trying to survive each day, and I'm not really living. 

I guess what I'm trying to say is, I need help. I need someone to talk to, someone who can help me figure out what's going on, and how to make it stop. I don't know what's wrong with me, or why I'm feeling this way. But I do know that I don't want to feel this way anymore. I want to be happy, and carefree, and just enjoy this time with my baby. But I don't know how to get there, and that's why I'm here.
